S01.title: Ashgrove data dictionary (release 2)
S01.what: Excel data dictionary for the Ashgrove Community Health Survey (synthetic), baseline, release 2: one record per participant, 15 variables on the Variables sheet and 4 special codes on the Codes sheet

S02.title: Ashgrove baseline questionnaire
S02.what: Interviewer-administered baseline questionnaire (Word, 21 paragraphs): sections A About you, B Smoking, C Women's health, D Health; 13 numbered questions; routing instructions in capitals at ¶8, ¶10, ¶13 and ¶21

D009.question: Is the data one table with one row per participant?
D009.answer: Yes — one table named baseline, one row per participant

D010.question: Which of your special codes mean "skipped by design"?
D010.answer: Only -6 (Not applicable) means skipped by design

D011.question: In the delivered data, can a cell be empty?
D011.answer: No — every cell holds an answer or a special code

D012.question: Are these the right topics for the dictionary?
D012.answer: Use these four topics: About you, Smoking, Women's health, Health

D013.question: How should we split the work into sittings?
D013.answer: One session: all four topics, in questionnaire order

D014.question: How exactly should participant IDs be written?

D016.question: What range of cigarettes per day should count as plausible?

D017.question: When someone refused (-7) or did not know (-9) whether they have smoked 100 cigarettes, or whether they smoke now, what do the smoking questions after it hold?

D018.question: Do the two smoking skip rules still match what the delivered data holds?
D018.answer: Yes — both match the delivered data

D020.question: Were women with no live births skipped on the first-birth age and breastfeeding questions?
D020.answer: Yes — I know this is how it was done

D021.question: When sex was refused (-7), what do the four women's-health questions hold?
D021.answer: Skipped like men: they hold -6 (Not applicable)

D022.question: Does the women-only rule still match what the delivered data holds?
D022.answer: Yes — it matches the delivered data

D024.question: When "ever told you have diabetes" was answered don't know (-9), what does the age at diagnosis hold?

D025.question: Does the diabetes follow-up rule still match what the delivered data holds?
D025.answer: Yes — it matches the delivered data

D027.question: Were ages above 85 changed in the delivered data?
D027.answer: Ages above 85 were top-coded to 85 in the 2024 release; nothing else changed.

D028.question: Were any ages at which people started smoking recoded in the 2024 cleaning?
D028.answer: Ages below 10 were recoded to -9 (don't know) as implausible, so real values run 10 to 80.

D029.question: Does a don't-know answer to "Do you smoke cigarettes now?" work like a refused or don't-know answer to the first smoking question?
D029.answer: Yes — a don't-know answer there also means the cigarette count was not asked: cigs_day is -6

D030.question: How precisely is body mass index delivered?
D030.answer: BMI was rounded to one decimal place in the 2024 release; nothing else changed.

D031.question: Your 2024 file has only 5 of the 15 variables. Is it the whole release or a partial extract?
D031.answer: A partial extract on purpose: the full release has all 15 variables (known and accepted)

D032.question: Every participant ID in your 2024 file fails the pattern "ACH followed by 4 digits". How are the IDs written in the delivered data?
D032.answer: The IDs are written differently from the dictionary: change the schema (describe the format in the note)

D033.question: 5 of the 40 records in your 2024 file have an age the schema rejects. What are they?
D033.answer: Errors or stray codes in the data: the data needs fixing

D034.question: Your 2024 file has a column named "canary" that is not in the dictionary. What is it?
D034.answer: A helper or test column that is not part of the study data (known and accepted)
